properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary can steal workload credentials, launch lookalike instances, compromise orchestration or inject/redirect agent actions.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Identity outlives workload; image/runtime provenance is unbound; shared keys span fleets; agent identity is confused with user intent; control plane mints arbitrary identity.
properties.MECHANISM: Use automatically issued short-lived workload credentials tied to orchestrator/platform evidence, resource/audience scope and deployment identity; distinguish user, agent and tool authority.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Cloud-native services, ephemeral workloads, CI/CD, service meshes, autonomous agents and machine-to-machine high-consequence operations.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a small single-host process tree, OS account/process isolation and local credentials may be sufficient.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Trusted issuance/orchestration, unique workload lifecycle, key protection, time and local authorization.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Machine identity does not replace responsible human/organisation ownership; user delegation is separately represented.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Issuers and platform administrators are bounded; agent/tool permissions are attenuated and cannot silently inherit all user authority.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Identity binds to code/image, deployment, environment and version where consequence warrants.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Observe identity issuance, unexpected geography/topology, delegation and use after workload termination.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Rebuild/revoke workloads and issuers without losing all service; retain clean bootstrap roots.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Eliminates many static secrets, narrows service authority and enables current policy/containment.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Platform/identity architect, service owner, CI/CD owner, agent platform owner and responder.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Control-plane compromise mints trusted identities; identity sprawl; certificates/tokens rotate but broad rights persist; provenance is asserted rather than verified.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Workload identity centralises trust and cannot prove software benignness. Agent identity/intent semantics remain immature.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From host certificates/shared accounts to ephemeral, provenance/context-linked workload identities and explicit user–agent–tool delegation chains.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Each non-human actor has a unique short-lived identity bound to current execution context and only the delegated authority needed for its task.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A service account, mesh certificate or agent name is not sufficient.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S109/S111 illustrate high leverage in cloud/enterprise identities; current AI guidance identifies agent/model/tool trust as a distinct translation but not a mature universal architecture.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Strong field-practice and guidance support exists for workloads; agentic systems have limited comparative/incident evidence and rapidly changing assumptions.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should machine identity be cryptographically and semantically bound to code, model, data, tool policy and the initiating human intent?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Emergency and break-glass authority with expiry, oversight and recovery
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: High-assurance operations, clinical/industrial access control and incident-response practice; a response to the availability limits of rigid least privilege.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Provide an exceptional, accountable route to exceed normal restrictions during defined emergencies.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Strict controls block life-, mission- or recovery-critical work, while hidden informal bypasses become permanent uncontrolled privilege.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Preserves availability, safety and recovery while bounding the security risk of exceptional authority.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Emergency may be genuine or adversary-induced; attacker may trigger or obtain break-glass access; normal identity/policy infrastructure may be unavailable.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Shared emergency credential leaks; use is unmonitored; exception never expires; trigger is vague; control-plane outage makes both normal and emergency access impossible.
properties.MECHANISM: Define narrow trigger, eligible actors, independent approval where feasible, short duration, exact scope, prominent monitoring, post-use review and automatic rollback; test offline/recovery use.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Safety/availability-critical operations, incident containment/reconstitution and rare cases where normal policy cannot meet consequence.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: No break-glass path for systems where all actions are easily reversible and normal privileged workflow remains available.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Explicit emergency scenarios, protected/accessible credentials, independent telemetry, policy owner and exercises.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Emergency identity proofing must work under degraded conditions without a universal weak fallback.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Authority to declare emergency and to exercise access are separated where feasible; all expansions expire.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Emergency policy/configuration is versioned and verified as part of deployment, not improvised.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Use creates high-priority tamper-resistant evidence and triggers review; covert use is a failure.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Post-emergency rekey/revocation and restoration of normal authority are mandatory.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents security controls from making systems unrecoverable while keeping exceptional access bounded and visible.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Incident commander, operations/safety owner, identity/security owner and risk acceptor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Permanent privileged accounts; rehearsed attackers know path; alerts ignored; emergency credentials inaccessible during outage; post-use rollback omitted.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Break-glass creates an attractive bypass and can normalise privilege. Evidence is domain-specific and operational exercises are essential.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From generic emergency accounts to scenario-specific, time/parameter-bound, independently observed and automatically expiring exceptional authority.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A tested exceptional path that minimises combined safety/availability/security harm and restores normal trust immediately after use.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A documented 'break glass' account without bounded trigger, monitoring and expiry is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Incident and sector guidance show the need for degraded operations and authority restoration; incident reports also show how privileged recovery channels can be decisive.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: No universal evidence establishes optimal approval or access design; threat and operational context dominate.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can offline emergency authority remain usable under infrastructure failure while resisting theft, coercion and false emergency declaration?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Secrets, keys and certificates as an authority lifecycle
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Cryptographic systems and PKI/key-management traditions; expanded into cloud secrets, signing identities, hardware roots and algorithm migration.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Generate, protect, distribute, use, rotate, revoke, archive/recover and destroy keys/secrets according to the authority they confer.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Encryption/signing mechanisms remain mathematically sound while operational keys leak, persist, are mis-scoped, cannot be revoked or make recovery impossible.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Confidentiality, authenticity and bounded control of identities, updates, transactions and protected data across the full system lifecycle.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary may steal credentials, compromise issuers/signers or management planes, observe accidental exposure, or exploit obsolete algorithms/protocols.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Long-lived shared secrets; secret in source/logs/images; one key serves many purposes; untested rotation; revocation does not propagate; lost key destroys availability; compromised signer remains trusted.
properties.MECHANISM: Minimise persistent secrets; use purpose/tenant/environment separation, protected generation/storage, short-lived issuance, inventory, rotation/revocation, emergency replacement, backup/recovery and cryptographic-agility plans.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any secret that grants consequential access, decrypts durable data, signs software/identity, anchors trust or cannot be cheaply replaced.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For local low-consequence ephemeral data, platform-provided credential stores and automatic short-lived credentials may be sufficient; avoid custom key infrastructure.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Accurate authority/secret inventory, trustworthy entropy/time, protected issuers/storage, deployable rotation and ownership.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Each secret is tied to a known principal/workload and assurance level; anonymous shared secrets are exceptional.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Key holders/issuers/signers have scoped authority and separation where consequence warrants.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Key identity/version, algorithm, environment, artifact/data scope and dependent configurations are traceable.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Use, anomalous access, issuance, expiry and failed rotation are observable without logging secret material.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Loss/compromise scenarios have tested rekey, data recovery and trust re-establishment; backups do not recreate revoked authority.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents operational cryptography from becoming permanent invisible privilege and makes compromise containment feasible.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Identity/PKI/key owner, application/service owner, build/release authority, operator and incident commander.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Rotation causes outage; old keys remain in caches/backups; hardware module becomes common mode; agility is paper-only; secret scanners create noise; encryption blocks recovery/forensics.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Cryptography relocates rather than eliminates trust. Hardware protection and certificate automation do not secure compromised issuers or authorised misuse.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From static passwords/keys to service-managed ephemeral credentials, distinct signing/decryption roots, transparent issuance evidence and planned post-quantum/algorithm migration.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Treat every secret/key as scoped, expiring authority with known consumers, provenance, revocation propagation and tested loss/compromise recovery.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A vault, HSM, encryption-at-rest badge or rotation ticket is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S109 demonstrates how a signing-key/identity-control failure can undermine broad cloud trust; S064 documents practical signing-key and workflow barriers.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Optimal rotation intervals and storage mechanisms are context-specific; stronger protection can increase availability and recovery concentration.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can large estates prove that revocation and emergency rotation reached every derived token, cache, artifact, backup and offline verifier?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Security requirements, invariants and unacceptable states
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Security-policy models, requirements engineering and systems-security engineering; misuse cases and assurance cases made claims more explicit.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Express security-relevant behaviour as testable constraints or invariants, including forbidden states and required recovery behaviour.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Vague requirements such as 'secure', 'use encryption' or 'follow best practice' cannot govern architecture, verification or risk acceptance.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Preservation of precisely stated confidentiality, integrity, authority, availability, authenticity, privacy or mission constraints.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary intentionally seeks boundary cases, composition gaps and state transitions omitted from ordinary functional requirements.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Requirement only names a control; invariant omits exceptional/recovery states; conflicts are hidden; test oracle is unavailable; requirement is stale.
properties.MECHANISM: Derive invariants from protected consequences and abuse cases; specify subjects, objects, transitions, assumptions, failure/recovery states and evidence; trace through architecture, implementation and operations.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High-consequence features, trust-boundary transitions, ambiguous policy, formal assurance targets and acceptance decisions.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-risk reversible features, a few executable negative checks and clear authorization rules can replace a large specification.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Protected consequence, bounded model, stable terminology, decision authority and feasible evidence/oracle.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity and principal semantics are explicit enough to state who may act.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Policy owner and risk acceptor are named; implementers cannot reinterpret obligation silently.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Requirement version maps to current design, code, deployment and supplier state.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Runtime/test evidence can discriminate invariant satisfaction; unknown/untestable claims are marked.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery and degraded states are part of the requirement, not assumed outside normal operation.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Provides a stable claim around which architecture, testing, monitoring and acceptance can align.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Requirements owner, architect, developer, tester/assessor, operator and risk acceptor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Over-formalisation freezes evolving needs; prose ambiguity persists; specifications omit environment; traceability becomes paperwork; controls pass while consequence fails.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Complete security specification is infeasible; adversarial creativity and emergent composition limit closure.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From policy labels and control requirements to consequence-linked invariants that include abuse, change, degraded operation and trust restoration.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A minimal, current set of decision-relevant security invariants with explicit assumptions, negative states and lifecycle evidence.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A requirements document, traceability matrix or compliance statement is optional and insufficient by itself.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S090 shows the value of precise properties while S091 demonstrates dependence on explicit assumptions; S082 documents practical overhead/currentness limits.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Formal precision does not guarantee correct or complete objectives; empirical comparative evidence for requirements methods is limited.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can security invariants remain precise yet evolvable when service composition, policies and adversary capabilities change continuously?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Security architecture and design review
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Trusted-system architecture and security-kernel work, later software-security architecture, threat modelling and systems-security engineering.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Challenge trust boundaries, privilege, data/authority flow, dependencies and failure paths before implementation fixes become expensive.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Local secure coding cannot repair an architecture that centralises trust, exposes unnecessary authority or lacks containment/recovery.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Prevents structural confidentiality, integrity, availability and blast-radius failures and creates an assurance/recovery design that can be implemented.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary exploits composition and authority paths, shared dependencies and exceptional states rather than only individual code defects.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Review occurs after decisions are irreversible; reviewers lack deployment context; checklist replaces adversarial reasoning; findings are not owned; architecture drifts.
properties.MECHANISM: Use objective/threat-driven review of trust/authority flows, TCB, isolation, common mode, abuse cases, updates, observability and recovery; record decisions and invalidation triggers.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: New system, material boundary/identity/dependency change, high-consequence feature, major migration or repeated incident class.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a small reversible change within an established boundary, a focused differential review of changed assumptions/interfaces is the cheap path.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Current architecture, capable reviewers, authority to change design and explicit review questions linked to consequences.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity issuers, proofing, workload identity and recovery are part of architecture, not external boxes.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Review establishes who grants/changes authority and where enforcement occurs.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Design reviewed must map to deployed configuration/build/dependency state; deviations are tracked.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Review specifies evidence needed to observe boundary violations and control failure.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Containment/reconstitution and safe degraded operation are design subjects.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Removes expensive structural vulnerabilities early and aligns later testing with real claims.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect, security engineer, product/platform owner, operators, assessors and risk acceptor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Review board ritual; diagram theatre; delayed delivery; reviewers share assumptions; threat model stale; local review misses emergent system behaviour.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Architecture review effectiveness is difficult to isolate empirically; excessive process can overwhelm low-risk change.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From central design sign-off to iterative, change-triggered, cross-lifecycle challenge with runtime and incident feedback.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Depth scales to consequence and novelty; every material trust/authority change receives independent-enough challenge, with decisions, assumptions and evidence consumers recorded.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A standing security review board or template is not required.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Major incident reviews S109–S113 expose architectural and process cascades that isolated defect scanning would not settle.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Mostly guidance and case-based support; controlled outcome evidence for design-review regimes is sparse.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which review triggers and representations maximise discriminatory value without recreating a heavyweight gate for every change?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Continuous secure lifecycle: security feedback everywhere
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Software-security/SDL traditions and secure product development lifecycles; modern SSDF, DevSecOps, secure-by-design and operational feedback.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Integrate security requirements, design, implementation, build, deployment, operation, response and decommissioning rather than attaching a final test.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Defects and insecure assumptions enter at every phase; a late gate cannot observe runtime configuration, supply chain or incident behaviour.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Reduces preventable vulnerabilities and preserves security claims as systems and threats change.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adaptive attackers exploit design, implementation, dependency, deployment, identity, operations and recovery weaknesses.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: 'Shift left' becomes scanner insertion; security gates delay delivery but runtime drift remains; ownership fragments; findings do not change architecture.
properties.MECHANISM: Place the cheapest discriminating control at each lifecycle point; feed runtime incidents and vulnerability intelligence back into design; bind release evidence to actual deployment; retire stale controls.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Products/services with ongoing change, exposed attack surface, dependencies and material consequence.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-risk/reversible changes, reuse established secure defaults and deterministic automated checks; escalate only when boundary, authority or consequence changes.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Product security ownership, version/configuration/provenance traceability, feedback channels and authority to remediate.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity/credential lifecycle is included from enrolment through revocation and retirement.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Security decisions and exceptions have owners and expiries across phases.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Source/build/release/deployment identity and change history support evidence continuity.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Telemetry, disclosure intake and incident learning close the feedback loop.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Patch, rollback, reconstitution and decommissioning paths are engineered and exercised.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents late-stage theatre and preserves current security through change.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Product/vendor, architects, developers, build/release, operations, security response and customers.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Process overload; many tools but no consequence reduction; gate bypass under urgency; security debt hidden; outsourced components outside lifecycle; evidence goes stale.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Integrated-programme benefits are often asserted by guidance/case studies rather than causal trials; mature practice must avoid tool/process accumulation.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From secure coding and final evaluation to continuous, risk-scaled trustworthiness engineering across product, supply chain, operation and retirement.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Security work occurs wherever a consequential assumption can be introduced or invalidated, with lightweight defaults for ordinary changes and deeper assurance for high-adversarial-pressure claims.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A DevSecOps platform, SDL checklist or 'shift left' slogan is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S087 shows how tool warnings can lose actionability; S113 shows deployment/update validation is as consequential as code-stage controls.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Comparative field evidence across complete lifecycle programmes remains limited and confounded by organisation size/capability.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which combinations of lifecycle practices produce independent marginal value, and where should security work deliberately stop for low-consequence change?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Change-aware threat-model and security-claim currentness
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Configuration management, continuous monitoring and threat-modelling criticism; modern cloud/CI/CD practice makes change invalidation central.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Reassess threat assumptions, boundaries and controls when architecture, authority, exposure, suppliers or adversary evidence changes.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A valid historical model or assessment remains 'green' after the system it described no longer exists.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Preserves relevance of design and assurance decisions under continuous system and threat change.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary exploits newly introduced paths, stale trust or delayed detection; change may be legitimate, malicious or environmental.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Annual review misses drift; model version not linked to deployment; updates add dependencies/permissions; external service semantics change silently.
properties.MECHANISM: Define explicit invalidation triggers, bind model/claims to configuration and provenance, monitor material drift, perform differential analysis and periodically challenge unchanged high-risk assumptions.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Boundary, privilege, dependency, exposed API, cryptographic, identity, deployment or recovery change; new exploitation/incident evidence.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Routine change entirely within a proven envelope uses automated invariant checks and records why the model remains valid.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Change inventory, configuration/provenance identity, ownership and an analysable security baseline.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity issuer/policy/recovery changes are model changes even without application-code change.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Changes to who can approve/deploy/administer are first-class triggers.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Claims carry version/commit/artifact/deployment/dependency identifiers and freshness metadata.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Continuous monitoring reveals divergence and model assumptions have observable proxies where possible.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Rollback/recovery changes are included; previous secure state is not assumed recoverable without proof.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents stale assurance and focuses review on deltas that can change adversarial paths.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Change owner, architect/threat modeller, release/platform operator, assessor and risk acceptor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Trigger flood; cosmetic model updates; unobserved external change; automation compares syntax not semantics; review latency drives bypass.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Complete semantic change detection is impossible; stable components can still face new adversary techniques without local change.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From periodic threat documents to configuration/provenance-bound living claims with event-driven reassessment and explicit freshness.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Security models and evidence identify the state they cover, their invalidators and last discriminating review; low-risk changes inherit only within stated envelopes.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Updating a document date or rerunning the same scanner is not model currentness.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S082 reports currentness difficulty; incidents S109–S112 show how changed dependencies/identity paths invalidate inherited assurance.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Research on continuous threat-model maintenance is immature; operational burden and false-trigger rates are not well characterised.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What minimal provenance and semantic-diff representation can reliably identify changes that invalidate a threat/security claim?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Secure implementation and memory-safe construction where justified
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Secure coding traditions, language/type safety, robust parsing and modern government memory-safety roadmaps.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Prevent exploitable implementation classes through safer languages, APIs, coding rules, input handling and privilege-aware construction.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Architecture can be sound while memory corruption, injection, unsafe deserialisation or error handling creates a bypass.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Reduces implementation vulnerabilities that permit code execution, data/authority violation or denial of service.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary controls malformed inputs or execution timing and targets implementation undefined behaviour; legacy/toolchain constraints apply.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Rules are untestable; unsafe escape hatches dominate; rewrite introduces semantic defects; memory safety is mistaken for complete security; generated code/dependencies remain unsafe.
properties.MECHANISM: Prefer memory-safe languages and safe libraries for new/high-exposure code; isolate unavoidable unsafe components; validate untrusted input; use compiler/runtime protections and targeted review/testing.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Internet-facing parsers, privileged code, high-consequence components, new codebases and components with recurring memory-safety defects.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-exposure scripts or constrained legacy patches, focused safe APIs, review and sandboxing may beat a rewrite; migration depth scales to consequence and lifecycle.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Supported toolchain/ecosystem, skilled developers, performance/real-time validation and accurate unsafe-code/dependency inventory.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Implementation must preserve identity and authorization semantics; memory safety does not prevent authorised misuse.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Unsafe/privileged operations require explicit authority and review.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Compiler/toolchain/build provenance and actual deployment protections are known.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Crash/sanitiser/fuzzing/telemetry reveal residual classes; production logging does not expose secrets.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Migration and rollback preserve service; compromised legacy components can be isolated/rebuilt.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Eliminates broad defect classes by construction and reduces scanner/review burden.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architecture/development leads, platform/toolchain owners, maintainers and risk acceptors.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Migration cost, ecosystem gaps, unsafe FFI, performance regressions, false security confidence and supply-chain shifts to new dependencies.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Memory safety does not solve logic, authorization, cryptographic, social or configuration flaws; comparative field estimates are ecosystem-dependent.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From coding checklists to defect-class elimination through language/platform design, bounded unsafe islands and secure defaults.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use construction techniques that deterministically remove material defect classes where exposure, consequence and maintenance horizon justify migration; assure residual unsafe boundaries.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A language mandate, secure-coding training completion or linter pass is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Government analyses attribute a large share of severe software flaws in studied ecosystems to memory-unsafety; fuzzing evidence S088 shows residual implementation bugs remain discoverable at scale.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Cross-language causal comparisons and rewrite risk are difficult; memory-safe platforms can still contain unsafe runtimes/FFI and logic defects.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which components deliver the highest net risk reduction from migration after accounting for rewrite defects, performance, support horizon and containment alternatives?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Code review and static analysis as bounded evidence
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Manual program review, compiler analysis and secure-development lifecycles; modern SAST and policy-as-code automation.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Inspect source/representation for specified defect classes before execution and use human review for contextual design/authority errors.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Implementation defects and dangerous changes can be detected cheaply before release, but no review/scanner covers all semantics or deployment states.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Reduces known implementation, dependency/API misuse, secret exposure and policy violations within the analysed scope.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary exploits defects represented in source/intermediate forms; tool rules and reviewers have bounded coverage and shared assumptions.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: False positives create suppression; false negatives/unsupported frameworks; reviewer fatigue; generated/build code differs; clean result becomes security proof.
properties.MECHANISM: Select high-precision rules tied to consequential classes, tune/triage with ownership, combine semantic human review for high-risk changes, measure suppression/escape and bind results to exact source/build.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Changes to exposed/privileged code, known dangerous patterns, policy/configuration and high-consequence authorization/crypto/update logic.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For small low-risk changes, compiler/type checks and a focused peer review may be enough; do not run broad noisy suites with no decision consumer.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Accurate language/framework model, maintained rules, reviewer competence, triage/remediation capacity and source provenance.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Review includes identity/authority logic rather than treating successful authentication as proof.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Reviewers can block/escalate consequential defects; suppressions/exceptions have scoped authority and expiry.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Tool version/configuration/source revision are recorded; generated/dependency/runtime configuration gaps are explicit.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Track actionable yield, escaped defects, suppression reasons and remediation—not raw findings alone.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Release/recovery process can revert a bad change and feed discovered classes back into rules/design.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Cheap repeatable detection for well-modelled classes and contextual challenge before deployment.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Developer, reviewer, security/tool owner, release decision-maker and assessor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Alert fatigue; gaming clean dashboards; broad rule disablement; same analyser in multiple gates; review is social approval without technical depth.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Scanner effectiveness varies materially by tool/class; suppression may be rational. Static evidence cannot establish runtime configuration or absence of adversarial paths.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From mandatory warning counts to calibrated, claim-specific analysis with explicit blind spots, independent evidence and feedback from escaped defects.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use deterministic high-signal static checks and risk-focused human review where they can change a decision; treat output as version-bound evidence, never a completeness claim.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A green SAST dashboard or two-person approval is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S087 empirically documents warning suppression and configuration/tool limits; scanner-comparison evidence illustrates non-interchangeability of tools.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Outcome evidence is tool/language/project-specific; disciplined static analysis can be highly effective for narrow classes despite broad averages.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should teams estimate marginal value and shared-assumption overlap among static tools and human review without rewarding finding volume?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Dynamic testing and fuzzing as bounded evidence
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Robustness/security testing and random/adversarial input generation; industrialised by coverage-guided continuous fuzzing.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Execute software against generated, malformed and adversarial inputs to discover crashes, memory corruption and specified behavioural violations.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Many input/state defects are difficult to reason about statically and emerge only under execution.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Finds concrete exploitable or reliability-relevant implementation defects before or after deployment within reachable tested states.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary controls inputs/timing/state; harness and oracle approximate real execution; unreachable environment paths remain outside evidence.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Poor harness never reaches critical code; crash count replaces severity; nondeterminism; sanitiser-only environment; fixed bugs do not repair root class; corpus stagnates.
properties.MECHANISM: Build realistic harnesses/oracles, instrument coverage, preserve/replay cases, prioritise high-exposure parsers/state machines, continuously fuzz and feed defect classes back into design/construction.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Untrusted parsers/protocols, memory-unsafe or complex stateful code, high-volume interfaces and components with suitable oracles.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For simple deterministic code with exhaustive input domain, property/unit tests or proof may be cheaper; low-exposure changes can reuse existing corpus.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Representative build/configuration, harness, oracle/sanitiser, compute budget, triage ownership and reproducible failures.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Authentication/authorization state and identities used by tests must reflect relevant paths.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Test infrastructure cannot exercise production authority or secrets unsafely; remediation decisions have owners.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Exact binary, instrumentation and environment are recorded; differences from production are explicit.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Coverage, unique defects, time-to-triage and escaped classes are observed without equating coverage with security.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Failed deployment can be rolled back; regression corpus protects repaired behaviour.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Strong practical defect discovery for broad input spaces and continuous regression at lower marginal cost.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Developer/test/security engineer, component owner and release assessor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Coverage gaming; duplicate crashes; false sense of completeness; impossible environment states; triage backlog; only crash properties tested.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Fuzzing cannot prove absence and may miss semantic authorization/business-logic flaws; empirical success is concentrated in fuzzable software.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From one-off random input tests to continuous coverage-guided, stateful, differential and property-oracle fuzzing integrated with remediation.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use fuzzing where a realistic harness and consequential oracle exist; report tested scope and remaining semantic/environment gaps.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A high execution count or zero crashes is not proof of security.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S088 analyses 23,907 OSS-Fuzz bugs across 316 projects, supporting strong defect-finding value while revealing project/class distributions.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Selection bias favours projects amenable to fuzzing; defect counts do not directly measure prevented compromise.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should fuzzing effort be allocated using exposure and consequence rather than coverage or crash volume alone?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Penetration testing and red teaming as scoped adversarial challenge
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Security testing, military exercises and red-team practice; later professional penetration testing and threat-emulation programmes.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Authorised independent-enough testers attempt to violate selected objectives using realistic adversarial paths and report exploitable chains.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Designers and automated tools share blind spots; integrated attack paths and operational response may fail despite component controls.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Discovers concrete exploitable paths, tests detection/response and challenges assumptions under bounded conditions.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Testers approximate specified adversary capability, access and time; legal/safety scope constrains action; absence of finding is not absence of path.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Narrow scope/window; known target; safe techniques omit destructive paths; report finding count; annual pass becomes certificate; fixes are local; red team shares intelligence/tools.
properties.MECHANISM: Define security claims and adversary profile, give realistic access where safe, assess prevention/detection/containment, preserve evidence, test root controls and retest; disclose exclusions.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Externally exposed/high-consequence systems, major architecture change, material uncertainty, regulatory/contractual requirement, or need to exercise response.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-risk reversible changes, targeted abuse tests or deterministic checks are cheaper; do not commission a broad annual ritual with no decision path.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Rules of engagement, safe environment, capable/independent testers, current configuration, remediation ownership and operational coordination.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Test identities/credentials and insider positions must match model; social techniques remain high-level and controlled.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Authorisation protects systems/users and defines stop conditions; testers must not possess hidden ability to declare the system secure.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Target build/deployment/configuration, seeded access and tool versions are recorded.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Detection/response observers distinguish missed, detected and contained actions; evidence is protected.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Exercises include restoration/revocation where safe, and findings feed architecture and playbooks.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Provides adversarially integrated evidence unavailable from checklists and many isolated scanners.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: System/risk owner, security architecture, operations/incident team, assessor and regulator/customer where applicable.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Scope theatre; finding inflation; zero findings misread; production harm; repeated known paths; perishable snapshot; consultant incentives; remediation closes tickets not invariants.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Attack space is effectively unbounded, testers are not the real adversary, and independence can be nominal. Comparative outcome evidence is limited.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From periodic vulnerability discovery to threat-informed, claim-specific purple/red exercises testing controls, telemetry, authority and recovery, combined with continuous bounded assurance.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use adversarial testing only when it can discriminate a material claim; state scope/time/access, treat findings as samples and require durable control learning.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A pentest report, badge or zero-finding result is not a security proof.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Scanner studies S085/S086 show bounded automated coverage; bug-bounty studies S095/S096 show external discovery value with concentration and incentive limitations.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Strong evidence exists for finding real defects, but evidence that annual tests/certificates reduce system-level loss is weak.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can adversarial exercises measure genuinely new discrimination and durable control improvement rather than repeated finding production?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Formal and property-based assurance for high-consequence claims
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Security models, theorem proving/model checking and verified kernels/compilers; modern industrial formal methods and access-policy verification.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Mathematically specify a security property and prove/model-check that a model or implementation satisfies it under explicit assumptions.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Testing samples behaviours and cannot establish exhaustive invariants over large state spaces; subtle concurrency/authority errors persist.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: High confidence in narrowly specified confidentiality, integrity, isolation, policy or functional-correctness properties.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary exploits any behaviour inside the formal scope; hardware, compiler, specification, environment and operational assumptions are explicitly outside or included.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Wrong/incomplete specification; model–implementation gap; proof excludes deployment/hardware/side channels; verified component used in unverified system; proof goes stale.
properties.MECHANISM: Select decision-critical invariant, minimise TCB, formalise assumptions/environment, use mechanised proof/model checking or property testing, validate correspondence to exact build/configuration, independently challenge specification.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Very high consequence, small stable trusted components, protocols/policies with tractable state, repeated defect classes or claims for which sampled testing is inadequate.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For ordinary low-consequence or rapidly changing code, type systems, deterministic tests, fuzzing and review may provide better value; prove the smallest necessary kernel/property.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Stable formal specification, skilled team/toolchain, bounded TCB/environment, provenance and maintenance commitment.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Principal/authority semantics must be faithfully formalised; proof of authentication protocol is not authorization correctness.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Who may change specification, proof assumptions and deployed policy is controlled.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Source/tool/compiler/build/configuration correspondence and proof artefact provenance are known.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Runtime attestation/monitoring can detect departure from proved envelope; model assumptions remain visible.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery/reconfiguration states are included or explicitly invalidate the proof.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Can provide exhaustive model-relative assurance and eliminate whole classes of subtle defects in critical mechanisms.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Architect/verifier, component owner, independent assessor, risk acceptor and downstream integrator.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Proof of wrong model; assumptions hidden; expertise/cost; brittle maintenance; success-case publication bias; proof badge used for whole system; environment drift.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Formal proof is not empirical security and cannot establish adversary/environment facts outside the model. Industrial adoption evidence is strong in cases but not universal.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From abstract policy models to mechanised, implementation-level and industrial proofs with explicit assumptions, verified toolchains and runtime/configuration binding.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Apply the strongest formal method to the smallest high-consequence claim where exhaustive evidence changes a decision; publish assumptions and maintain correspondence.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A model, theorem-prover use or certification claim is not whole-system assurance.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S090 establishes a landmark kernel verification result; S091 explicitly limits its assurance envelope; S093 documents industrial applications and barriers.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Comparative causal outcome and cost-effectiveness evidence is limited; specification completeness and deployment reality remain dominant uncertainties.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can proof obligations and deployment/provenance evidence be maintained economically through rapid updates and compositional supplier changes?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Independent, diverse and current-configuration-bound assurance evidence
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Evaluation/certification traditions, independent testing and modern continuous assessment; refined by recognition of shared assumptions and stale evidence.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Support a security claim with evidence sufficiently independent in people, method, data and failure mode, and tied to the state actually deployed.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Many reviews/tools can project the same model error, benchmark blind spot or stale configuration while appearing mutually corroborating.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Reduces false confidence and gives decision-makers evidence that discriminates materially different failure hypotheses.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary benefits from correlated blind spots, evaluator incentives and changes after assessment; evidence producers may be compromised or mistaken.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Nominally independent assessors use identical scanners/checklists; tests share oracle; certificate covers old version; evidence author also owns acceptance; multiple weak signals are aggregated as certainty.
properties.MECHANISM: Define claim and threat assumptions; select complementary evidence types; record independence and shared dependencies; bind evidence to artifact/configuration/provenance/time; expire/reassess after invalidating change.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High-consequence claims, certification, external trust, major releases, common-mode risk and any completeness/security assertion.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-risk reversible change, one high-signal deterministic check plus provenance may be enough; do not multiply checks without expected discrimination.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Explicit claim, evidence consumers, source identities, configuration/provenance mapping, assessor authority and conflict-of-interest disclosure.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity of evidence producer, signer and tested principals is known; evaluator identity alone does not establish independence.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Acceptance authority is distinct enough from implementation/evidence production for consequence; exceptions are visible.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Every result records source/build/artifact/deployment/policy/tool/version and validity conditions.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Evidence freshness, coverage, disagreements and invalidation triggers are observable.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Rollback/recovery evidence is exercised separately from preventive evidence where its failure mode differs.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents certificate/scanner/test accumulation from masquerading as robust assurance and concentrates cost on informative evidence.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Assessor, risk acceptor, customer/procurer, release authority, regulator and operator.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Independence becomes organisational label; evidence diversity adds noise; conflicting results are averaged; version binding omitted; assurance latency blocks urgent patches.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: True independence is expensive and sometimes impossible where all evidence depends on the same hardware/cloud/toolchain. More evidence can reduce rather than increase decision clarity.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From one-time evaluation levels to claim-specific assurance portfolios with provenance, explicit common assumptions, continuous invalidation and adversarial challenge.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use the minimum mutually informative evidence set adequate to consequence; disclose model/environment gaps and automatically invalidate stale state-bound claims.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A certificate, assessor logo, tool count or 'independent review' statement is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Tool-comparison and suppression studies S085–S087 show materially different and correlated coverage; S091 demonstrates why even strong proof needs assumption disclosure.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Independence and marginal information are hard to quantify; standards largely prescribe assessment discipline rather than prove optimal portfolios.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What practical measure can identify shared assumptions and expected information gain before commissioning another review, scanner or test?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Vulnerability discovery and coordinated disclosure intake
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Bug reporting, CERT coordination, vulnerability databases and secure-development response; formalised in disclosure policies and supplier obligations.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Provide authorised channels to receive, validate, coordinate, remediate and disclose externally or internally discovered security defects.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Researchers/users find defects but cannot report safely; duplicated secrecy, premature disclosure or unowned reports prolong exposure.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Faster recognition and remediation of real vulnerabilities while balancing user protection, transparency and exploit window.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Benign researchers, customers and adversaries may discover the same issue; reports can be malicious, mistaken or sensitive.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: No monitored channel; legal threats suppress reporting; triage backlog; duplicate/invalid reports dominate; disclosure dates detach from patch readiness; bounty incentives favour quantity.
properties.MECHANISM: Publish scope/contact/safe-harbour terms, authenticate communications, triage and reproduce, assign ownership/severity/exposure, coordinate suppliers/users, issue fixes/advisories and learn recurring classes.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Externally used products/services, complex supply chains, security-relevant APIs and organisations likely to receive independent findings.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a tiny private system, a clear internal contact and response procedure may suffice; a paid public bounty is not mandatory.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Response team, legal/process clarity, secure communication, inventory/affectedness, patch/update capability and user notification.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Reporter identity may remain pseudonymous; authenticity of advisories and affected product identity are critical.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Only authorised owners accept risk or disclose; researchers do not silently gain production authority.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Reports bind to exact product/version/configuration and resulting fix/advisory provenance.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Track acknowledgement, validation, time to protective action, recurrence and affected deployment—not report count alone.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Emergency remediation, rollback and user recovery plans exist before public exposure when feasible.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Extends discovery beyond internal testing and converts external knowledge into durable product improvement.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Product security response, supplier/maintainer, release owner, customers/operators and disclosure coordinator.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Volume gaming; researcher exclusion; patch withheld; incomplete affectedness; legal chill; public CVE/ticket closure precedes deployed remediation.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Bug bounties favour discoverable defect classes and popular products; disclosure timing has genuine competing risks; report volume is not security.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From informal contact/CVE assignment to coordinated product-security response linked to dependency identity, safe harbour, secure updates and root-cause learning.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: A reliable, respectful intake-to-protection loop whose metrics centre affected users, remediation and recurrence—not bounty/CVE counts.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A vulnerability disclosure policy page, CVE assignment or bounty programme is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Bug-bounty studies S095/S096 support external discovery value but show concentration/incentive effects; KEV S073 distinguishes observed exploitation from mere listing.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Field causal evidence on disclosure-policy design is limited and selection effects are strong.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should disclosure timing and public detail be chosen when patch availability, active exploitation and downstream supply-chain affectedness diverge?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Exposure-, reachability- and consequence-aware vulnerability prioritisation
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Vulnerability databases/scoring and patch management; refined by exploit evidence, asset context, reachability and mission consequence.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Prioritise remediation using technical severity plus actual exposure, exploitability, reachable path, compensating controls, affected consequence and remediation risk.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: CVSS or finding count is mistaken for system risk, causing scarce effort to chase high scores while exploitable consequential paths persist.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Faster reduction of meaningful exploit paths and harm under finite remediation capacity.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary chooses reachable and useful weaknesses, may chain lower-severity flaws and adapts to public exploit/patch information.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Component version detection is wrong; vulnerable code is unreachable yet consumes effort; low-score chain ignored; asset inventory stale; KEV/EPSS treated as certainty; patch risk omitted.
properties.MECHANISM: Join accurate component/deployment identity with exposure, reachability, exploit evidence, privilege/path, compensating controls and consequence; include uncertainty and remediation/availability cost.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Non-trivial backlog, heterogeneous assets, delayed patches, transitive dependencies or conflict between patch urgency and stability.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a small inventory with a safely deployable fix and material exposure, patch directly after basic validation; elaborate scoring adds no value.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Current inventory, topology/runtime reachability, consequence model, vulnerability data quality and patch/change authority.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Privilege/identity needed for exploitation is represented; assumed unauthenticated/authenticated access is current.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Risk acceptance and exceptions have named authority and expiry.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Version/configuration/dependency and deployed patch status are verified rather than inferred from ticket state.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Observe exploit attempts, exposure, patch rollout, exceptions and residual vulnerable paths.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Rollback/mitigation is prepared where patch can damage availability; containment supports delayed remediation.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Directs constrained engineering effort toward vulnerabilities that can produce real protected consequences.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Vulnerability/product owner, asset/service owner, operations/change authority and risk acceptor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: False precision; data sparsity; scanner disagreement; reachability misses dynamic/reflection paths; exploit prediction changes; business criticality becomes subjective; backlog gaming.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Severity remains useful as a portable technical input but is not organisational risk. Reachability tools can create false negatives; exploitation can change rapidly.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From CVE/CVSS queues and patch SLAs to current affectedness plus exploit-path/consequence prioritisation with explicit uncertainty and exception expiry.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use the cheapest context that changes order—known exploitation, exposure, reachable vulnerable function, privilege and consequence—without claiming exact risk probabilities.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A CVSS threshold, vulnerability count or closed ticket is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S076/S077 find that exploitation is concentrated and severity alone poorly discriminates; S068/S069 show SBOM/scanner inconsistency and affectedness false positives.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Predictive/reachability evidence is ecosystem- and time-dependent; unknown exploitation and chained paths remain.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can prioritisation remain auditable and uncertainty-aware without becoming an opaque proprietary score that is itself gamed?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Remediation verification and security-exception expiry
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Patch/change management and audit follow-up; evolved from ticket closure to state verification and time-bounded residual-risk decisions.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Verify that a fix or compensating control removed the actual exposure in the deployed system and ensure deferred risk is re-decided before assumptions expire.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Source patch or closed ticket does not prove every deployed instance, vulnerable path or derivative artifact is corrected.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Prevents persistent known exposure, incomplete fleet remediation and permanent emergency exceptions.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary continues exploiting unpatched/incorrectly patched instances or waits for compensating controls/exceptions to lapse.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Patch applied to wrong version; vulnerable code remains in image/cache; scanner false negative; mitigation bypass; exception auto-renewed; rollback reintroduces flaw.
properties.MECHANISM: Bind remediation to affected asset/artifact, verify deployed state and exploit/path closure, monitor rollout/rollback, set exception owner/rationale/compensating controls/expiry and retest.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Material vulnerability, broad fleet, complex dependency/update paths, compensating mitigation or any deferred remediation.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a small controlled deployment, a version/hash/config check and one targeted regression test may settle closure.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Accurate affectedness, deployment inventory, update authority, test oracle, exception governance and observability.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Credential/identity changes are verified across all sessions/tokens/issuers where part of remediation.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Only named risk authority can accept residual exposure; operational tickets cannot silently do so.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Fix source, build artifact, signature/provenance, deployed version/config and rollback image are linked.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Coverage of rollout, residual vulnerable instances, control operation and exception age are visible.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Rollback/failure plan avoids choosing between unknown security state and unavailable service.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Converts remediation effort into evidence that adversarial opportunity actually decreased.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Vulnerability owner, release/operations, assessor, service owner and risk acceptor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Retest repeats same flawed scanner; partial fleet invisible; patch creates regression; exception owner leaves; mitigation only moves path; metric rewards speed over correctness.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Verification costs can delay urgent fixes; no test proves absence of alternate paths. Patch and service stability trade-offs are real.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From patch-ticket closure and SLA to provenance/configuration-bound affectedness closure, staged validation and expiring residual-risk decisions.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Closure requires evidence about the current deployed exposure and affected consequence; exceptions are temporary hypotheses with explicit invalidators.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A status field 'remediated' or scanner disappearance alone is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S110 illustrates broad dependency remediation/coordination; S113 demonstrates patch/update validation can itself create systemic failure.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Optimal verification depth depends on urgency, exploit activity and deployment reversibility; empirical evidence on exception governance is limited.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What minimum evidence establishes fleet-wide closure without delaying urgent mitigation, especially across opaque suppliers and ephemeral instances?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Dependency identity, current inventory and affectedness
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Configuration/software inventory and vulnerability management; modern SBOM and dependency-graph practice.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Know which exact direct/transitive components, versions, sources and relationships are present in each deliverable/deployment, and determine whether a reported issue actually affects them.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Unknown, duplicated or misidentified dependencies prevent timely impact analysis and allow stale/abandoned/vulnerable code to persist.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Rapid, accurate response to supplier compromise/vulnerability/licence-support events and reduced ungoverned transitive trust.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary may compromise maintainers/registries/dependencies or exploit known defects; inventory generators and metadata may be incomplete or manipulated.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: SBOM omits generated/vendored/runtime dependencies; tools disagree; version/identity aliases; inventory goes stale; presence is mistaken for reachable affectedness.
properties.MECHANISM: Generate inventory from authoritative build/resolution evidence, include direct/transitive and relevant runtime/firmware elements, record tool/context/unknowns, update with releases, verify samples and join to reachability/consequence.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Third-party code, large dependency graph, externally distributed products, regulated sectors, rapid vulnerability response or supplier due diligence.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a small vendored/pinned codebase, deterministic lockfile/hash plus documented manual dependencies may be cheaper than a formal SBOM exchange.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Reproducible dependency resolution, component identifiers/hashes, build/runtime visibility, ownership and update process.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Supplier/maintainer identities are recorded but do not prove trustworthiness.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Who may add/update dependencies and approve unresolved/abandoned components is bounded.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Inventory binds to source/build/artifact/deployment and generator/version; currentness/coverage and unknown fields are explicit.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Detect newly introduced, missing, end-of-life and vulnerable dependencies and observe deployment affectedness.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery/rebuild can replace compromised dependencies from trusted sources and revoke affected releases.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Shrinks time to affectedness decisions and exposes transitive maintenance/provenance risk.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Developer/build owner, product-security response, supplier/customer, vulnerability manager and assessor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Format completion ceremony; inconsistent tools; enormous noisy inventories; unavailable proprietary components; stale documents; component naming ambiguity; reachability false confidence.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: SBOM existence does not establish completeness, provenance, exploitability or trust. Recent empirical evidence shows severe cross-tool inconsistency.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From static package lists to artifact-specific, generation-context-rich inventory linked to build provenance, runtime reachability, lifecycle status and affectedness.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Dependency identity can be reconstructed for the exact artifact/state, quality/unknowns are explicit, and inventory directly supports change/vulnerability/supplier decisions.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: An SBOM file or standard format alone is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S068 generated 55,444 SBOMs with six tools across 3,287 repositories and found very low package/licence consistency; S069 reports high affectedness noise in studied repositories.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Empirical studies cover selected ecosystems/tools and one is a preprint; inventory remains valuable despite quality limits.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can inventory completeness and affectedness be independently measured across build-time, runtime, generated, vendored, firmware and external-service dependencies?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Source/build provenance, build isolation and source-to-binary correspondence
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Compiler/toolchain trust and reproducible-build traditions; operationalised by in-toto, SLSA, isolated CI/CD and attestations.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Establish who/what produced an artifact, from which inputs and process, under what isolated conditions, and whether delivered bytes correspond to reviewed source.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Trusted source can produce untrusted output through compromised builders, dependencies, compilers, credentials or substitution.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Integrity and traceability of software/firmware from source through build and distribution, enabling compromise detection and reconstruction.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary may control repository, maintainer, CI worker, dependency registry, toolchain, build secret or artifact store.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Self-attested provenance; compromised issuer; mutable build environment; hidden network input; unreproducible artifact; reproducibility confirms malicious source; source review not linked to binary.
properties.MECHANISM: Pin/identify inputs and toolchains, isolate/hermetically constrain builds, use ephemeral builders and least privilege, generate signed attestations from the build service, independently verify policy and use reproducibility/source comparison where feasible.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Externally distributed or privileged artifacts, automated deployments, high-value supply chains, third-party builds and recovery images.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a small internal low-risk tool, a clean controlled build, pinned hashes and recorded source/artifact digest may suffice; full SLSA infrastructure is optional.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Protected source and build identities, deterministic dependency resolution, trustworthy time/signing, verifier policy and ownership.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Builder/maintainer identities are distinct and revocable; identity alone does not establish process integrity.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Build, release and policy authorities are separated/limited according to consequence.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: All inputs, tool versions, build steps, environment, outputs and attestations bind cryptographically to exact artifact.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Verification failures, unexpected inputs/network access and provenance gaps are visible; logs are protected.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Clean-room rebuild and key/pipeline reconstitution can restore trusted production after compromise.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Closes a major source-to-deployment trust gap and narrows investigation/rebuild scope.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Build/release/platform owner, supplier/customer verifier, product security and incident responder.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Attestation is signed by compromised build plane; framework level becomes badge; hermeticity breaks needed updates; reproducibility too costly/non-deterministic; toolchain trust infinite regress.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Provenance records facts claimed by an issuer; they do not prove source benignness or builder honesty unless independently anchored. Reproducibility is equivalence, not security.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From signatures and reproducible builds to policy-verifiable, identity-bound provenance across isolated build steps plus independent rebuilding for selected high-consequence artifacts.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Artifact acceptance depends on verified provenance and bounded builder authority appropriate to consequence, with explicit residual toolchain/hardware assumptions.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A provenance record, SLSA level or reproducible-build badge alone is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S111 (SolarWinds) and S112 (XZ) establish repository/build/maintainer paths as system-scale threats; S064 documents real signing-adoption barriers.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Field evidence is incident- and practice-led; comparative causal evidence for individual framework levels is limited.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can verifier-independent evidence cover opaque hosted builders, compilers, firmware and generated dependencies without prohibitive latency?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Artifact and release authenticity with signer/build-authority validation
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Digital signatures, PKI and trusted update/release systems; refined by transparency, role separation and provenance verification.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Verify that an artifact/release was authorised for a specific product/channel/version by a currently trusted signer and has not been substituted or replayed.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Unsigned or weakly bound artifacts can be replaced, but a valid signature can also authenticate a compromised or over-authorised release process.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Integrity/authenticity of deployed software, configuration, policy and firmware plus accountable release authority.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary may tamper in transit/storage, steal signing keys, compromise release account/build plane, replay/rollback older signed artifacts or abuse delegated signing.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Signature checked but signer authority/audience/channel/version not; key compromise; transparency not monitored; signing happens on developer workstation; malicious signed update; rollback to vulnerable release.
properties.MECHANISM: Use protected and separated release keys, threshold/role delegation where warranted, artifact/product/channel/version binding, transparency/attestation, expiry/revocation, rollback protection and independent policy verification.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Distributed software/configuration, privileged agents, firmware, recovery media and cross-organisational delivery.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For local low-risk artifacts, authenticated repository plus hash/provenance and controlled deployment may suffice; public PKI/transparency not always needed.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Key lifecycle, canonical artifact identity, protected release process, verifier policy and update/recovery mechanism.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Signer/build-service identity is current and distinct from arbitrary developer identity.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Release authority is scoped by product/channel/environment and separated from build/policy where consequence warrants.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Signature covers exact bytes/metadata and is linked to provenance, dependency/configuration and intended environment.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Unexpected signer, key use, log inconsistency, downgrade and deployment divergence are observable.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Compromise response revokes signer, identifies affected releases and reconstitutes clean signing/update roots.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents substitution and unauthorised release while making release compromise investigable/containable.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Release/build authority, verifier/deployment platform, customer/operator and incident responder.
