properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Valid signature creates false trust; private key copied; old signed vulnerable artifact accepted; transparency log not checked; emergency key inaccessible; revocation bricks offline devices.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Signing establishes origin under a key, not build/source security. Central signing services are high-value common mode and offline availability complicates revocation.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From binary signing to role-separated, provenance-linked, transparent and rollback-resistant release authorization with tested signer compromise recovery.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Accept artifacts only when bytes, provenance, intended channel/version and current bounded signer authority all satisfy policy.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A signature badge or signed file alone is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S109 shows trusted signing authority can be compromised/misused; S111/S112 show authorised-looking supply-chain artifacts can carry compromise.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Strong cryptographic mechanism evidence contrasts with limited comparative evidence for operational signing programmes and documented adoption barriers.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How should offline/embedded verifiers handle signer revocation and rollback protection during prolonged control-plane or time-source failure?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Secure update, rollback/downgrade protection and staged rollout
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Patch management, signed software distribution and secure update frameworks; modern continuous delivery adds canarying, health checks and rapid rollback.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Deliver authentic, authorised and safe changes, prevent forced reversion to known-vulnerable state, and control deployment blast radius.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Delayed updates preserve exposure; rushed or compromised updates can create fleet-wide security/availability failure; ordinary rollback can reintroduce vulnerabilities.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Timely remediation without unauthorised code/configuration, systemic outage or persistent downgrade.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary may block/freeze, replay, substitute or compromise updates; benign defective updates are also material system threats.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Signature only; no version freshness; central update pushes globally; canary unrepresentative; rollback uses vulnerable image; emergency patch bypasses validation; clients cannot update.
properties.MECHANISM: Authenticate and authorise update metadata/artifact, protect roles/keys, enforce freshness/rollback rules, stage/canary, monitor security/service health, support safe rollback/forward fix and maintain offline/recovery channels.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Externally exposed or fleet software, privileged agents, firmware/OT/medical devices and urgent vulnerabilities.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a small reversible service with immutable deployment, one controlled update plus health/security check and known-good image may be enough.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Asset/version inventory, release provenance, protected update channel, representative tests, monitoring, operational authority and recovery capacity.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Update service/client identities and channel authorisation are current; device ownership/recovery is defined.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Who may release, stage, halt, rollback or override is separated/bounded.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Update metadata, artifact, signer, build provenance, target environment and installed state are linked.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Rollout coverage, failures, security regressions, unexpected signer/version and blocked clients are observable.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Known-good recovery sources are protected and not vulnerable to the same compromise; downgrade exceptions are explicit.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Balances exposure reduction with availability/stability and limits common-mode deployment failure.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Product/release owner, operations/SRE, security response, device/service owner and incident commander.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Patch pressure causes outage; rollback defeats remediation; staged users remain exposed; old clients unsupported; update plane is compromised; health checks miss security defects.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Urgent patching and thorough validation conflict; no rollout strategy eliminates zero-day or common-mode risk. Update availability varies by sector.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From signed patches and maintenance windows to provenance-verified, freshness-enforced, staged, observable and recoverable continuous updates.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use consequence-proportionate validation and staged exposure while preserving rapid containment; rollback policy distinguishes availability recovery from unsafe downgrade.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A signed update, successful CI build or 'patch applied' ticket is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S110 shows emergency ecosystem-wide update need; S113 shows a trusted content update causing major outage, establishing staged validation/common-mode constraints.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Incident evidence is strong; comparative evidence for rollout configurations and optimal patch delay is context-specific.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can systems quantify acceptable exposure during staged rollout while ensuring rollback does not restore known exploitable state?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Secure configuration baselines, desired state and drift detection
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Trusted-system configuration control, hardening/checklists and configuration management; evolved through infrastructure/policy as code and continuous monitoring.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Define a versioned secure desired state, authorise changes and detect/remediate divergence in actual runtime configuration.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Correct code and assessment can be defeated by permissive deployment, disabled logging, exposed service, weak policy or emergency override.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Preserves intended authorization, isolation, update and observability properties in the real environment.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary may alter configuration or exploit benign drift; operators and automated platforms also introduce unreviewed differences.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Baseline copied without context; compliance reports syntactic state not effective authority; IaC differs from runtime; auto-remediation causes outage; exceptions persist; ephemeral resources evade inventory.
properties.MECHANISM: Use consequence-specific baselines, declarative desired state, peer/automated checks, authorised change, runtime reconciliation, exception expiry and semantic security-impact review.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Production/privileged/shared systems, regulated baselines, large fleets, cloud/containers, frequent deployment and repeated misconfiguration.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a simple isolated system, a small versioned config plus deterministic startup check may suffice; full policy-as-code platform is optional.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Known system inventory, configuration ownership, reliable state collection, tested remediation and availability constraints.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity/authorization configuration is included, including effective transitive roles and recovery settings.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Only authorised changes can modify desired/actual state; automation identity is least-privileged.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Baseline, policy code, environment, image/artifact and deployed observations are traceable.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Drift, failed reconciliation, emergency overrides and effective policy outcomes are visible.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Rollback/rebuild uses protected baseline and does not erase incident evidence or restore obsolete insecurity.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Reduces persistent misconfiguration and makes assurance current rather than document-bound.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Platform/operations, security architecture, service owner, assessor and incident responder.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Checklist compliance theatre; false positives; hidden manual changes; central policy error propagates fleet-wide; auto-remediation fights legitimate adaptation; baseline lags threats.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Baseline compliance does not prove runtime safety or security; strict uniformity can harm resilience and domain operations.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From hardening guides and periodic scans to provenance-linked desired state, continuous semantic drift detection and bounded, observable exceptions.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Maintain the minimum secure state needed for current objectives, verify actual effect, and retire controls/settings whose threat or consumer has disappeared.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A benchmark percentage, configuration checklist or IaC repository is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S113 shows fleet-wide configuration/update mechanisms can become common-mode availability risks; incident reviews show logging/identity configuration gaps matter.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Semantic drift and outcome evidence are difficult; automated enforcement can produce correlated failure.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can drift systems distinguish dangerous semantic change from legitimate adaptive variance without centralising catastrophic authority?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Runtime detection, observability and tamper-resistant security evidence
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Audit trails/accountability in trusted systems, intrusion detection and log management; expanded to distributed telemetry and continuous monitoring.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Collect sufficient trustworthy evidence of security-relevant state and actions to detect misuse, investigate claims and trigger containment.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Preventive controls fail silently; attackers persist because consequential actions, boundary crossings or control degradation are not visible.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Shorter detection/decision time, accountable operations, evidence-preserving response and validation of threat/control assumptions.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary may evade, disable, forge or flood telemetry; legitimate high-volume events create noise; logging itself can leak secrets/privacy.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Logs omit identity/parameters; central collector compromised; alerts overwhelm; anomaly model drifts; coverage unknown; data retention violates privacy; alert firing is mistaken for containment.
properties.MECHANISM: Derive telemetry from security objectives/abuse paths; protect integrity/time/access, minimise sensitive content, map coverage and blind spots, tune actionable detection, correlate identity/config/provenance and test with exercises/incidents.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High-value authority, exposed boundaries, privileged/admin actions, update/build systems, regulated evidence and recovery/forensics needs.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-consequence local work, structured audit of consequential state changes and deterministic integrity checks may be enough; avoid broad behavioural surveillance.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Defined detection consumers/playbooks, trustworthy clocks/identities, protected collection, retention/privacy policy and operational triage capacity.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Events carry trustworthy principal/workload/session identity; identity-system compromise is detectable or an explicit blind spot.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Who may change logging/detection and who may suppress alerts is bounded and independently observable where warranted.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Telemetry identifies system/configuration/artifact/policy version; gaps after change invalidate coverage claims.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Coverage, data loss, alert quality, response latency and blind spots are measured; detection is regularly challenged.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Evidence survives containment/rebuild; recovery systems retain necessary forensic/decision records without restoring compromised collectors.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Turns unknown control failure into actionable state and supports current assurance, containment and learning.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Detection engineering/SOC, service owner, incident commander, privacy/legal owner and assessor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Alert fatigue; vanity dashboards; secret/PII leakage; high storage cost; attacker poisons or disables data; central telemetry outage; no response authority.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Detection cannot compensate for weak prevention and may create surveillance/privacy/security risk. Outcome attribution and anomaly false-positive rates are context-dependent.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From generic logging and signatures to claim-driven, identity/provenance-aware, tamper-evident telemetry with known coverage and direct containment consumers.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Observe the smallest security-relevant evidence set that can discriminate material states and drive authorised action, while protecting data and monitoring the monitor.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A SIEM deployment, log volume or alert count is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S109 identified logging/visibility failures as part of a consequential cloud intrusion; S099 supports warning/alert habituation constraints.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Detection effectiveness varies with threat, data and staffing; sparse ground truth limits comparative claims.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can detection coverage and evidence integrity be established when the identity, management or telemetry plane itself is compromised?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Incident declaration, response authority and containment
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Military/emergency operations and computer incident response; modern CSIRT/SOC and lifecycle risk-management integration.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Define who can declare an incident, obtain evidence, isolate systems, suspend authority, communicate and coordinate service decisions.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Signals are observed but no one has authority/context to act; fragmented teams delay containment while compromise spreads.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Limits adversary dwell, blast radius and consequential harm while preserving accountable service/safety decisions.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary is active, adaptive and may exploit coordination delay, ambiguous ownership and response tooling; false alarms also impose cost.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Alert never becomes incident; roles conflict; containment destroys evidence or safety; communications leak; playbook assumes unavailable identity/network; business owner blocks necessary action.
properties.MECHANISM: Predefine thresholds, command roles, legal/technical/business interfaces, containment options and stop conditions; exercise degraded scenarios; grant bounded emergency authority; maintain secure communications.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Material indication of compromise, control loss, high-confidence exploit activity, supplier compromise or unexplained security invariant violation.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a small low-consequence event, one accountable operator can isolate, preserve minimal evidence and escalate; a full command structure is unnecessary.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Current contacts/asset dependencies, exercised playbooks, containment mechanisms, executive/risk support, legal/privacy/safety coordination.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Responder identities and privileged credentials remain available and distinguishable during compromise.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Declaration, isolation, shutdown, disclosure and restoration authorities are explicit and proportionate.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Playbooks/tooling match current architecture/configuration and can operate when primary systems are unavailable.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Telemetry reaches decision-makers; response actions and evidence custody are recorded.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Containment is selected with reconstitution and service continuity in mind; clean channels and recovery resources exist.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Converts detection into timely bounded action and reduces uncontrolled propagation/conflicting decisions.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Incident commander, service/product owners, security operations, legal/privacy, safety/continuity and executive risk authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Paper plan unexercised; response permissions too weak or broad; destructive containment; hidden dependencies; overclassification; premature closure; outsourced responders lack context.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Formal incident processes can slow obvious containment; aggressive isolation can create availability/safety harm. Incident labels and timing metrics are gameable.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From IT ticket escalation to exercised, cross-functional, threat-informed command with pre-authorised containment and recovery coordination.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Decision rights, communication and containment options are designed before crisis, exercised under degraded trust, and scaled to consequence.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: An incident-response plan, retained consultant or closed incident ticket is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: CSRB and CISA incident reports S109–S111 demonstrate cascades amplified by visibility, coordination and authority failures.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Incident studies are rich but selected and retrospective; controlled comparative evidence on response structures is limited.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which pre-authorisations minimise response delay without enabling abuse or unsafe automated containment?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Credential and authority revocation across control planes
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Account/key revocation and incident containment; broadened to tokens, federation, workload identity, cloud sessions, signing and delegated agents.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Remove compromised or no-longer-intended authority everywhere it can still act, including derived sessions, keys, tokens and downstream delegations.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Disabling one account leaves active tokens, API keys, certificates, service roles, signed artifacts or persistence in other planes.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Stops continued authorised-looking action after identity/authority compromise and bounds containment time.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary already controls valid authority and may have minted derivatives, altered policy or established persistence.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Directory account disabled but sessions remain; signing key revoked but artifacts accepted; federated issuer continues; emergency access persists; downstream agent credentials unknown.
properties.MECHANISM: Inventory authority derivation, revoke at issuer and enforcement points, invalidate sessions/keys/certs, rotate dependencies, inspect policy/persistence, verify propagation and re-establish clean identity roots.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Credential theft, insider departure, identity/provider compromise, supplier/signing compromise, privilege error or incident containment.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a single local account with no derived credentials, disable, rotate and verify one enforcement point.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Authority/dependency graph, issuer/enforcer control, emergency access, reliable propagation and clean administrative channel.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Compromised identities and legitimate replacement identities are distinguishable; recovery proofing is sound.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Revocation authority is protected and cannot be blocked/overridden by the compromised principal.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Token/key/policy/artifact versions and all dependent deployments are traceable.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Use after revocation, propagation failures and unexpected issuances are visible.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Clean identity/keys and bounded service restoration exist; revocation does not permanently lock out recovery.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Removes a common gap between incident action and actual attacker authority.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Identity/key/platform owners, incident commander, application/resource owners and release/security teams.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Incomplete inventory; revocation latency; offline verifiers; attacker changed root policy; massive rotation outage; revocation itself abused for denial of service.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Global instantaneous revocation is often impossible; central revocation creates availability/common-mode risk.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From disabling accounts to graph-aware invalidation of human, workload, signing, token and delegated authority plus verification of residual effects.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Containment proves that all material derived authority is expired/revoked or isolated, then rebuilds identity trust from clean roots.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: An account-disabled status or password reset is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S109 shows how signing/token authority can survive or evade ordinary identity assumptions; ransomware guidance S114 calls for broad credential containment.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Revocation completeness and propagation are architecture-specific; evidence is mostly mechanism/incident based.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can a live authority graph be maintained across SaaS, cloud, offline devices, build systems and agent delegations without itself becoming a sensitive common-mode target?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Recovery and reconstitution from trusted sources with trust re-establishment
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Backup/disaster recovery joined with cyber-resilience, secure boot/update and incident forensics.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Restore required service and data from protected, validated sources while proving that compromised authority, code, configuration and persistence are removed.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A backup exists but is corrupted, reachable by the attacker, restores vulnerable state or cannot establish when trust was lost.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Restores mission/service availability and integrity after compromise without reintroducing the adversary or untrusted state.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary may corrupt/encrypt backups, recovery credentials, images, update channels and logs or persist in identity/management planes.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Restore point already compromised; backup untested; clean room shares identity; rebuilding host leaves cloud tokens/policy; urgency skips validation; forensics blocks recovery or vice versa.
properties.MECHANISM: Maintain offline/immutable/segmented recovery material, known-good source/build/configuration, independent credentials/control path, regular restore exercises, compromise-timeline/affectedness analysis, rekey/revoke and verify invariants before reconnecting.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Ransomware/destructive attack, management/identity/supply-chain compromise, uncertain fleet state or critical corruption.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a small reversible stateless service, rebuild from verified source/artifact and restore minimal data with a targeted integrity check.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Protected backups, clean bootstrap roots, source/build provenance, asset/dependency map, recovery objectives, staffing and alternate communications.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery identities/keys are separate, protected and usable offline/degraded; compromised identities are not reused.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Authority to select restore point, destroy/rebuild and reconnect is explicit.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Recovery images/data/configuration/build inputs have known provenance/version and are tested.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery progress, integrity checks, residual compromise and reconnection decisions are auditable.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: This property is itself the recovery prerequisite: exercises verify time, completeness, isolation and trust restoration.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Turns prevention failure from existential/unbounded loss into bounded service degradation and trustworthy reconstitution.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Continuity/service owner, incident commander, platform/data/identity owners, forensics and risk authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Backup-only theatre; untested restore; shared admin/online storage; stale dependencies; recovery time dominates mission tolerance; validation too weak; restored system still vulnerable.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Recovery is expensive and domain-specific; immutable backups can impede privacy deletion or rapid update. Trust can rarely be proven absolutely after deep hardware/identity compromise.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From availability backup/restore to cyber recovery that reconstructs identity, provenance, configuration, dependencies and evidence from a separately protected trust base.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Recovery succeeds only when required service returns and current objectives/invariants are re-established from independently trustworthy material under a bounded residual-risk decision.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A backup, rebuilt host or service-up metric is not proof that trust is restored.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Current ransomware guidance S114/S120 stresses offline, immutable, segmented and tested backups; major incident reports show identity/build/update roots may also require reconstitution.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Strong guidance and incident support; comparative evidence for clean-room architectures and trust-restoration metrics is limited.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What evidence is sufficient to declare a recovered environment trustworthy when the initial compromise time and depth remain uncertain?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Cyber resilience and graceful degradation
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Survivable systems, continuity and resilience traditions; NIST systems-security engineering formalised anticipate, withstand, recover and adapt.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Design the system to continue essential functions, contain damage, recover and adapt when prevention fails under adversarial pressure.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Perfect prevention is unattainable; tightly coupled systems can lose all mission value after one compromised dependency or defensive shutdown.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Continuity of essential service, bounded harm and timely trustworthy recovery during/after attack.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adaptive adversary may compromise components, disrupt dependencies, deceive monitoring and target recovery; benign faults coexist.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Resilience becomes vague excuse for preventable vulnerabilities; redundancy shares common mode; degraded mode violates security/safety; recovery objective untested; adaptation expands attack surface.
properties.MECHANISM: Define essential functions and degradation priorities; compartmentalise, diversify selectively, reserve capacity, use alternate control/communications, pre-plan reconstitution and measure exercises against consequence.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: High mission/availability consequence, persistent adversary, critical infrastructure, cloud concentration or systems that cannot simply stop.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-consequence/recreatable services, rapid immutable rebuild and acceptable outage may be cheaper than complex fail-operational architecture.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Explicit mission priorities, dependency/common-mode analysis, operational exercises, recovery resources and authority.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Degraded identity/authorization semantics are designed; offline/local control is bounded.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Who can enter/exit degraded modes and adapt controls is explicit.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Fallback systems, data, code and configuration have current provenance and do not preserve obsolete vulnerabilities.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Observe degradation, resource health, adversarial adaptation and whether essential functions remain within bounds.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery/reconstitution objectives and clean roots are central, not appendices.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents a single compromise from becoming total mission failure and turns recovery into an engineered capability.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Mission/service owner, architect, continuity/resilience, operations, incident command and risk authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Unmeasurable slogans; costly redundancy; hidden common dependencies; failover propagates compromise; resilient service continues unsafe/unauthorised actions; exercises unrealistic.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Resilience can normalise weak prevention and its metrics are immature; diversity/complexity can worsen security.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From disaster recovery and redundancy to adversary-aware, trust-preserving degradation, containment, reconstitution and learning.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Resilience is specified in terms of essential consequence, adversary model, allowable degradation, trusted fallback and tested restoration—not generic uptime.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A resilience strategy, backup count or high-availability topology is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Incident and ransomware evidence shows continuity/recovery paths are active attack surfaces; S113 demonstrates common-mode defensive update can defeat availability.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Field/incident support is strong; quantitative resilience measures and comparative architecture evidence remain weak.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can resilience be measured without rewarding systems that remain available while silently losing integrity, confidentiality or safety?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Incident learning and root-invariant repair
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Accident/incident review, vulnerability root-cause analysis and secure-development feedback loops.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Use incidents and near misses to repair the enabling architectural/control invariant, update assumptions and verify recurrence resistance.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Teams close individual tickets or patch indicators while the shared authority, process or design weakness continues across products.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Reduces recurrence and transfers hard-won adversarial evidence into design, assurance, detection and recovery.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversaries repeat or vary proven techniques; organisational incentives favour rapid closure and narrow attribution.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Blame individual; confidential report never reaches engineering; local fix; lessons too generic; metrics reward closure time; recommendations unowned/stale.
properties.MECHANISM: Construct causal/contributing-factor account, map compromised objectives/assumptions, identify systemic/common-mode conditions, assign corrective actions and verification, update threat models/tests/defaults and monitor recurrence.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Material incident, repeated vulnerability class, near miss with high potential consequence, assurance escape or recovery exercise failure.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a small isolated defect, add a regression test and repair the narrow root class; a formal postmortem is unnecessary.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Evidence preservation, psychological/legal safety, cross-functional authority, action ownership and longitudinal tracking.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity/authority misuse and recovery paths are included rather than attributing all events to user error.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Owners can change architecture/process and accept unresolved systemic risk.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Lessons bind to affected products/configurations/dependencies and identify broader population.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Corrective action and recurrence indicators are observable; sensitive evidence remains protected.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Exercises validate that containment/recovery changes work under the learned scenario.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Converts adversary experience into durable reduction of future exploitability and response cost.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Incident owner, architects/developers, product/vendor leadership, risk authority and affected customers/regulators where appropriate.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Hindsight bias; incomplete evidence; secrecy/liability pressure; recommendation backlog; monocausal narrative; fixes create new risk; recurrence hard to measure.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Post-incident recommendations are observational and can overfit one event; transparency and operational secrecy conflict.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From incident closure and patching to evidence-preserving system learning that changes models, defaults, assurance and recovery across the affected population.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Closure requires verified repair or explicit acceptance of the exploited invariant, not merely eradication of the observed instance.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A postmortem document, lesson-learned meeting or closed action list is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: CSRB reports S109/S110 and CISA incidents S111/S113 expose cascades and systemic recommendations beyond single vulnerability fixes.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Retrospective evidence is subject to incomplete observability and selection; outcome validation of recommendations is often absent.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can incident-learning actions be tested for causal recurrence reduction without waiting for another rare adversarial event?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Secure-by-design and secure-by-default product responsibility
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Software security and SDL, economics of externalities, then CISA/partner secure-by-design programmes and product-security regulation/procurement.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Place primary responsibility for eliminating preventable vulnerability classes and unsafe defaults on the producer with design/control knowledge, rather than downstream users.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Vendors externalise hardening, patching and insecure-default cost to customers who cannot inspect or fix architecture.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Fleet-scale reduction of preventable defects, unsafe setup and operational burden; clearer lifecycle support and disclosure responsibility.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversaries exploit widely deployed default/design weaknesses and long-tail customers unable to harden quickly.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Marketing pledge without engineering change; security feature is paid add-on; legacy compatibility preserved indefinitely; vendor metrics opaque; customer assumes all risk transferred.
properties.MECHANISM: Design out recurring classes, ship safe defaults, remove universal/default credentials, provide logging/update/identity capabilities, publish lifecycle/support, accept disclosure and measure customer-impacting outcomes.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Mass-market, internet-facing, critical, enterprise platform or component whose producer controls architecture/defaults/update channel.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For bespoke internal low-risk tools, local owner responsibility may be sufficient; formal public pledge/regulatory programme is optional.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Product governance, lifecycle funding, engineering competence, customer feedback and ability to update safely.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Strong authentication/recovery is available by default; identity burden is not shifted to customer configuration alone.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Vendor executives/product owners hold authority to change defaults and retire unsafe compatibility; customers retain local risk decisions.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Default/support claims identify product/version/configuration and supply-chain evidence.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Vendor can observe vulnerability/incident patterns and customer adoption without disproportionate data collection.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Support/update/recovery commitments allow customers to restore and migrate; end-of-life is explicit.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Moves scalable prevention to the party best able to alter code/defaults and reduces downstream ceremony.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Vendor/product leadership, engineering/security, customers/procurers and regulators.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Branding/pledges; unsupported legacy; security lock-in/surveillance; forced updates cause outages; producer hides evidence; small vendors face disproportionate cost.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Current programmes are largely normative; optimal allocation of liability/cost and causal outcome evidence remain contested.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From customer hardening and secure-coding programmes to product responsibility for design, defaults, lifecycle evidence, support and safe decommissioning.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: The producer removes foreseeable classes/default hazards and provides verifiable secure operation/recovery, while customers retain context-specific configuration and consequence ownership.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A pledge, trust centre, certification or premium security SKU is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Economic analyses S102 and user-burden work S097/S098 support responsibility reallocation; incidents show producer-controlled shared systems can create enormous external consequences.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Most direct evidence is policy, economics and incidents rather than controlled comparisons; producer responsibility can centralise control/privacy risk.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which product-security outcomes can be independently verified without incentivising under-reporting, surveillance or exclusion of small suppliers?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Security metrics and proxy-gaming resistance
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Audit/risk management and vulnerability metrics; sharpened by security economics, risk-matrix criticism and empirical scanner/SBOM evidence.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Use measures only when their relationship to a decision, protected consequence and uncertainty is understood; monitor incentives and independent outcome evidence.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Counts and scores become targets, so teams optimise vulnerabilities closed, control coverage, training completion or alert volume without reducing adversarial risk.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: More reliable prioritisation and governance; prevention of false confidence and resource diversion.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adaptive organisations and vendors game visible metrics; sparse/biased incident data and changing adversaries weaken inference.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: CVSS becomes risk; scanner/tool changes improve dashboard; suppressed findings hidden; MTTR encourages premature closure; phishing click rate blames users; maturity score lacks outcome validity.
properties.MECHANISM: Define decision/use and causal hypothesis, validate data/coverage, separate technical severity from consequence, report uncertainty and missingness, use counter-metrics/audits, inspect gaming and retire metrics without consumers.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Any metric that allocates resources, declares security, compares units/vendors or creates incentives.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a local deterministic state, measure the state directly (e.g. signed artifact hash, revocation propagation) rather than invent a maturity score.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Explicit consumer/decision, trustworthy data provenance, stable definitions, adversarial/gaming review and ability to act.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity of subjects/tools/assets is consistent; privacy-preserving aggregation avoids harmful surveillance.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Metric owner cannot redefine thresholds/denominators silently; acceptance authority sees uncertainty.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Data binds to current population/configuration/tool version and records missing/unknown cases.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Monitor data quality, denominator coverage, behavioural response and divergence from incidents/outcomes.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Metrics include recovery/availability costs where they govern security decisions.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents measurement ceremony and focuses evidence on discriminating security states.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Risk/security leadership, product/service owners, operators, assessors, regulators/customers.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: False precision; unreported denominator; survivorship/selection bias; correlated tools; tail risk; causal attribution; target gaming; privacy harm.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Cyber outcome data are sparse and selected; many metrics are useful locally but not transferable. Quantitative models can still aid decisions when uncertainty is explicit.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From counts/compliance scores to decision-specific evidence with current population, uncertainty, causal humility and Goodhart-resistant governance.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: No metric may stand in for security: it must identify population, state, decision, uncertainty, incentives and independent validation.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A dashboard, scorecard, risk matrix, CVSS distribution or maturity level is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S068/S069 show tool/inventory/affectedness instability; S076/S077 show severity and exploitation distributions diverge; S100 limits interpretation of training measures.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Direct cyber loss and counterfactual data are limited; rejecting all metrics would also impair learning and prioritisation.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which metrics have demonstrated predictive or decision value across contexts, and how can denominator/configuration changes be exposed automatically?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Risk, uncertainty and security-depth proportionality with a cheap path
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Risk management, security economics and lifecycle tailoring; modern secure engineering recognises consequence, exposure, adversary and reversibility differences.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Scale architecture, assurance and process depth to protected consequence, credible exposure, reversibility, novelty and adversary capability.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Universal heavyweight security wastes capacity and induces bypass, while uniform minimalism under-protects high-consequence systems.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Maximum marginal security value under finite resources without converting low-risk work into compliance queues.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversaries concentrate where payoff/exposure is high; uncertainty and rare tail outcomes remain; process itself can create availability/delivery risk.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Risk matrix false precision; 'low risk' used to avoid controls; high risk triggers every tool; cheap path lacks guardrails; reversible changes have irreversible data/authority effects.
properties.MECHANISM: Define escalation triggers and minimum invariants; choose cheapest deterministic check first; add independent assurance only when expected to change decision; record uncertainty/residual risk and reassess after change.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: All work, with deep paths for high consequence/exposure/irreversibility, novel trust/authority, weak observability or persistent capable adversaries.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Established low-exposure, easily rolled-back change within a proven envelope uses secure defaults, provenance, focused tests and monitoring—no bespoke threat model/pentest board.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Reliable consequence/threat classification, bounded change envelope, rollback/recovery and authority that cannot self-exempt silently.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity/authority changes usually escalate even when code delta is small.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Risk/exception authority is separated from convenience incentives and decisions expire.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Cheap path requires exact change/artifact/configuration identity and proof that assumptions remain inside envelope.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Post-deployment signals can reveal misclassification and trigger escalation.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Reversibility is tested and includes data, authority, supplier and customer effects—not only code rollback.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Preserves attention for high-adversarial-pressure claims and reduces process-induced insecurity.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Product/system owner, security architect, change/release authority and risk acceptor.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Subjective risk tiers; underestimated unknowns; bureaucratic scoring; low-risk path becomes loophole; deep path tool accumulation; overconfidence in rollback.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Rare events and sparse data make proportionality uncertain; formal proof may be cheap for some properties while manual review is not. There is no universal depth formula.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From uniform control baselines to trigger-based, claim-specific and reversible security assurance with explicit low-cost inheritance paths.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Every change gets a minimal security invariant/provenance check; depth escalates only for stated consequence, threat, trust-boundary, irreversibility or uncertainty triggers.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A risk score, tier label or blanket waiver is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Threat-modelling and user-burden evidence S082/S098 shows process cost matters; S113 demonstrates small-looking shared updates can have irreversible fleet consequence.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Empirical data cannot supply universal thresholds; proportionality is governance-sensitive and gameable.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Can escalation triggers be validated against escaped incidents and process cost without becoming another maturity/checklist score?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Explicit security–privacy–safety–availability–usability tension adjudication
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Systems/security risk management and domain co-engineering; sharpened by usable security, critical infrastructure and medical-device practice.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Make competing objectives and failure directions explicit and choose context-dependent controls, degraded modes and evidence rather than declaring security automatically dominant.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: A locally strong control produces outage, unsafe physical behaviour, privacy invasion, unrecoverable encryption or unusable workarounds.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Preserves combined mission/human trustworthiness and prevents security controls from becoming another hazardous failure source.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversaries may exploit both weak protection and defensive responses; benign failures and human constraints interact.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Fail closed blocks care/control; logging leaks secrets/PII; rapid patch breaks service; segmentation blocks emergency coordination; encryption defeats recovery; telemetry centralises sensitive data.
properties.MECHANISM: Model both sides' consequences and adversarial paths; assign joint owners; design bounded hybrid modes (break-glass, privacy-minimised logs, staged patch, local fallback); test normal/degraded/recovery conditions.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Cyber-physical/medical/OT, critical availability, sensitive personal data, central identity/telemetry, strict isolation or irreversible key/update decisions.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For ordinary systems with aligned objectives, record the relevant side constraint and use established defaults; no multi-board process needed.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Cross-domain expertise, consequence ownership, realistic scenarios, conflict escalation and evidence of trade-off performance.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity and logging use only necessary personal data; emergency proofing remains possible.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: No single discipline can silently waive another's protected consequence; residual conflict has authorised owner.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Control/configuration versions and operating modes are traceable.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Observe both security and competing outcomes, including denial, bypass, privacy exposure and safety effect.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery plans reconcile evidence preservation with rapid restoration and key/data availability.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents security theatre that merely transfers risk and improves deployability of strong controls.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Security, privacy, safety, availability/operations, user representatives and mission/risk owner.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Committee deadlock; every conflict becomes exception; qualitative balancing hides power; attacker exploits fallback; privacy/safety invoked to preserve insecure legacy.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: No universal optimum exists and values/legal duties differ. Joint process can become bureaucratic without decision authority.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From one-dimensional CIA/control selection to explicit multi-consequence engineering with scenario-specific hybrid resolution and residual-risk visibility.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: For each material conflict, identify failure directions, context favouring each property, bounded hybrid, monitoring and unresolved risk; scale process to consequence.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A policy statement that all requirements are 'balanced' is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Medical/OT guidance S045/S117 establishes safety/availability interactions; S113 demonstrates security-update mechanisms can cause widespread availability failure.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Trade-off resolutions are domain- and value-dependent; empirical generalisation is limited.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can residual cross-property risk be represented without collapsing qualitatively different human, mission and privacy consequences into one arbitrary score?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Lifecycle retirement, decommissioning and stale-control removal
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: System/configuration management, key/media disposal and secure lifecycle practice; modern cloud/dependency/product end-of-life makes retirement continuous.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Remove obsolete systems, identities, interfaces, data, secrets, dependencies and controls safely when their consumer or threat context disappears.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Abandoned assets and dormant privilege remain exposed and unpatched; obsolete controls create friction, complexity and common-mode failure.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Reduces residual attack surface, data exposure, maintenance burden and misleading assurance while preserving required records/recovery.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary discovers forgotten systems/accounts/domains/keys/dependencies; decommissioning itself can leak data or break needed services.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Asset still reachable; DNS/cloud storage takeover; secret in backup; dependency unsupported; retention violated; removal breaks hidden consumer; stale control retained for audit score.
properties.MECHANISM: Identify consumers/dependencies, authorise retirement, migrate/retain required data, revoke identities/keys, erase or archive verifiably, remove routes/policy, update models/evidence and monitor for reappearance.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: End-of-life product/service, unused integration/account, unsupported dependency, expired exception, changed threat/obligation or control with no decision consumer.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For ephemeral resources, automatic expiry and reconciled desired state are the cheap path.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Inventory/dependency map, data/legal retention rules, owner authority, deletion/revocation capability and rollback contingency.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: All human/workload/service identities and recovery channels tied to retired object are closed or reassigned deliberately.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Owner authorises decommissioning and accepts residual archival obligations.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Actual deployed instances, artifacts, backups, DNS/registries and downstream copies are traced.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Post-retirement scanning/monitoring detects residual access, credentials or resurrection.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery/archival needs are preserved without retaining live exploitable authority.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Eliminates forgotten exposure and complexity and prevents obsolete ceremony from consuming assurance capacity.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Asset/product owner, platform/identity/data owner, security, legal/privacy and operations.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Incomplete inventory; hidden consumer outage; 'soft delete'; keys remain; backups impossible to purge; audit requirements preserve useless controls; unsupported system cannot migrate.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Secure deletion/retirement can conflict with forensics, legal retention, resilience and historical reproducibility.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From end-of-project disposal to continuous expiry and verified removal of cloud resources, identities, dependencies, evidence and controls.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Every security-relevant object/control has owner, consumer, support horizon and retirement condition; decommissioning closes authority and verifies residual state.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: An asset marked decommissioned or archived ticket is not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Supply-chain and vulnerability evidence shows unsupported/transitive components remain consequential; incident experience makes forgotten identities/assets recurring exposure classes.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Empirical outcome data on decommissioning programmes are sparse; complete erasure across replicas/backups is technically and legally difficult.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can organisations establish complete retirement across opaque SaaS, backups, downstream artifacts and derived credentials without destroying required recovery/evidence?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Compliance mapping with outcome/evidence separation
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Trusted-system evaluation, control catalogues, audit and management-system standards; modern risk frameworks and continuous assessment.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Map applicable obligations to implemented controls, responsible owners and current evidence without treating completion or certification as security outcome proof.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Legal/contractual duties are missed, duplicated or detached from implementation; conversely, control compliance is mistaken for adversarial effectiveness.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Demonstrable obligation coverage, accountable governance and reusable evidence while preserving independent judgement about actual risk.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary does not respect compliance scope; assessors and organisations may optimise auditable artifacts; systems change after evidence collection.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Control matrix has no configuration binding; scope excludes critical suppliers; inherited control assumptions false; exceptions hidden; audit pass overrides incident evidence.
properties.MECHANISM: Identify obligation and scope, map to security objective/control/owner/current evidence, record inheritance and gaps, test effectiveness where consequence warrants, expire evidence after change and report residual risk separately.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Regulated/contractual environments, external assurance, complex obligation sets or shared controls.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For an unregulated small system, record relevant legal/customer requirements directly in objectives; no large control matrix is needed.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Authoritative obligation interpretation, system scope/population, evidence provenance, assessment competence and risk authority.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Identity of assessed organisation/system/evidence producer is precise; certification scope is not assumed transitive.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Compliance assessor does not silently accept security risk; waivers and residual risk have authorised owners.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Evidence links to exact configuration, artifact, period and inherited provider state.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Continuous monitoring and incidents can invalidate compliant status; missing coverage is visible.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Obligations include incident/recovery and evidence retention where applicable.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Prevents legal/contractual omissions and reduces duplicate evidence work without replacing engineering judgement.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Compliance/legal, system/control owners, independent assessor, risk acceptor, customer/regulator.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Checkbox audit; sampled evidence generalised; stale certificate; control-count target; auditor conflict; management-system certification treated as secure product; paperwork overwhelms small change.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Standards/certificates establish requirements or assessment processes, not empirical optimality or absence of compromise. Compliance can still be necessary and valuable.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From static control checklists and evaluation grades to risk/objective-linked, configuration-current obligation/evidence maps with explicit non-equivalence to outcomes.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use compliance as a bounded source of obligations and evidence discipline; separately establish adversarial claims and current effectiveness.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: A certificate, audit pass, control coverage percentage or completed matrix is not a general security property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Incident reports including S109 show that organisations/products with extensive controls can still suffer cascaded failures; evaluation standards themselves delimit scope and assumptions.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Comparative certification-outcome studies are confounded and mixed; compliance may improve baseline governance without proving security.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which compliance evidence has independent predictive value for specific adversarial outcomes after controlling for organisation size, sector and reporting bias?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Security training and awareness as supplementary control
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Personnel security and user education; modern awareness, phishing simulation and secure-development training.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Provide role- and task-relevant knowledge/practice so people can recognise exceptional risk, use controls and report incidents.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Users/developers/operators face novel or ambiguous decisions not fully eliminable through automation/design.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: Improves recognition, reporting and correct use of remaining human-mediated controls while supporting secure organisational coordination.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Adversary targets human cognition/workflow; training transfer decays and attackers adapt; participants have legitimate task pressures.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Completion is outcome; generic annual content; simulated-phish punishment; click metrics; overtraining habituates; training substitutes for phishing-resistant authentication or safe defaults.
properties.MECHANISM: Train only on consequential decisions people genuinely control, make scenarios role-specific and spaced, provide immediate legitimate actions/reporting, measure durable task/incident outcomes and redesign recurrent failure out of the workflow.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Residual human judgement, privileged operations, incident reporting, secure development tasks and new threat/control changes.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: If a deterministic safe default or phishing-resistant mechanism removes the decision, use that instead; low-risk users need concise just-in-time guidance.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Usable controls, management support, reporting safety, realistic content, privacy-respecting evaluation and remediation authority.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Training cannot compensate for weak proofing/authentication; recovery and support staff need role-specific identity knowledge.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: People must have legitimate authority/path to act; otherwise awareness without capability is futile.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Training content matches actual deployed tools/policies and is updated after changes/incidents.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Observe reporting, task performance, near misses and support/workaround patterns—not just attendance or simulated clicks.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Exercises include degraded/incident roles and recovery; training itself is not a recovery capability.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Can improve performance for irreducibly human tasks and create shared incident vocabulary at modest cost.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Workforce/product leadership, security education, control owners, users/operators and incident teams.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Blame culture; surveillance; weak transfer; repeated simulation normalises deception; inaccessible content; high false-positive reporting burden.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Large field evidence shows some common training forms have limited effects; behavioural improvement does not directly establish reduced compromise.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From annual awareness and 'human firewall' rhetoric to role-specific practice embedded in usable controls, with design responsibility and measured residual tasks.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use training only for decisions that remain legitimately human; pair it with phishing-resistant/default controls and treat recurrent errors as design evidence.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: Completion certificates, click-rate targets or 'security culture' scores are not the property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S099 shows habituation to repeated warnings; S100's 19,500-person field study found limited effect for common embedded phishing training conditions.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Training interventions and outcome measures are heterogeneous; some targeted programmes may work well in specific roles.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which tasks remain best allocated to human judgement, and which training outcomes predict materially reduced compromise rather than short-term test performance?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: SBOM artifact alone as proof of supply-chain trust
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Modern software-supply-chain inventory programmes; admitted to the denominator as a ceremonial candidate to be explicitly rejected.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Possess an SBOM in a recognised format and infer that the dependency graph and supply chain are trustworthy.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Attempts to solve opaque dependency composition and vulnerability response through a portable inventory artifact.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: At most supports inventory exchange and affectedness investigation; it does not by itself protect any objective.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Assumes generator completeness/accuracy, honest source/build process, stable identifiers, current artifact binding and equivalence between presence and exploitability.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Missing/transitive/generated dependencies; tool disagreement; stale document; malicious component faithfully listed; signed SBOM from compromised builder; no reachability/provenance/currentness.
properties.MECHANISM: Retain the underlying P35/P36 properties: reconstruct exact dependencies, quality/unknowns, provenance and affectedness for a current artifact; use SBOM as one implementation.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Use an SBOM when ecosystem exchange, procurement, regulation or rapid response benefits justify it.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For small/pinned builds, lockfiles, hashes and build provenance may provide sufficient inventory; no SBOM format required.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Accurate generator context, artifact identity, source/build evidence and update process.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Supplier/tool identities are inputs, not trust conclusions.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: No SBOM producer may self-authorise acceptance of its own opaque supply chain without verifier policy.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: SBOM version/hash/generation tool/context binds to exact artifact and release.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Quality, coverage, drift and disagreement are measurable; affectedness is separately assessed.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery/rebuild requires trusted sources/builds, which the SBOM does not provide.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Inventory can materially reduce response latency when high quality; the rejected inference prevents ceremony.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Customer/procurer, product-security response, build owner and supplier manager.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Format compliance dominates accuracy; document goes stale; scanners inflate findings; procurement treats file presence as trust.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Recent empirical studies show severe tool inconsistency and false-positive affectedness; guidance itself specifies unknowns/currentness rather than trust proof.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: Inventory artifact emerged as useful standardisation but is being refined toward generation context, signatures, hashes, quality and affectedness, while provenance remains separate.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: An SBOM is optional evidence serving P35; trust requires verified dependency, build/provenance, authority and current affectedness chains.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The named candidate is ceremony, not a retained general property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: S068 found low cross-tool package/licence consistency at large scale; S069 reports extensive false-positive affectedness in its studied corpus.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Tooling and standards are improving, and high-quality SBOMs can be valuable; rejection applies only to the trust inference, not inventory.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which independently testable SBOM quality/coverage thresholds are feasible across languages, build systems and firmware?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Zero-trust programme or vendor branding as a general property
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Perimeter critique and identity-centric architecture programmes; admitted as a ceremonial label while its transferable mechanisms are retained elsewhere.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Adopt a product stack, maturity label or slogan that 'trusts nothing' and infer improved security.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Attempts to address implicit network trust, remote/cloud distribution and compromised internal locations.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: No intrinsic payoff; underlying P03/P04/P06/P16–P19/P40 mechanisms can protect resource-specific authorization and visibility.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Assumes central identity, telemetry, policy and enforcement remain trustworthy/available; credential compromise and legacy paths persist.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Network segmentation rebranded; every request still inherits broad roles; policy complexity; surveillance; control-plane common mode; vendor lock-in; availability failure.
properties.MECHANISM: Retain no implicit authorisation from location, resource-specific/current decisions, bounded identity/workload authority, segmentation and telemetry with explicit control-plane compromise/recovery.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Use a zero-trust architecture programme when it helps govern a genuinely distributed migration and its dependencies/costs are explicit.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For a simple bounded system, implement least privilege and complete mediation directly; no programme, maturity model or vendor suite required.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Accurate resource/identity inventory, enforcement coverage, policy usability, telemetry and resilient identity/control plane.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Current identity/device/workload evidence must be appropriate; authenticated compromise remains possible.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Policy administration and exception authority are bounded; resource owners retain intent.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Policy/enforcement configuration and issuer/telemetry provenance are current.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Coverage and central-plane failure are observable; logging respects privacy.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Local/degraded authorization and recovery from identity/policy compromise are designed.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Can remove implicit location trust and improve authority visibility when architecture actually changes.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Enterprise architect, identity/network/platform owners, service owners, privacy/continuity and risk authority.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Branding without resource mediation; continuous authentication prompts; central failure; legacy bypass; policy sprawl; high cost; inferred trust from vendor telemetry.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Zero trust does not mean zero assumptions. Evidence is mainly architecture guidance and implementation experience, not proof that branded programmes outperform alternatives.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From perimeter-based trust to resource/context/identity-centric authorization; mature practice treats location as one weak signal and models central dependencies.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Underlying property: network/topological location never substitutes for current bounded authorization; all remaining trust assumptions are explicit.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The programme name, maturity score and product stack are optional and not a general property.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Cloud identity incident S109 and common-mode update failure S113 show why central identity/control-plane assumptions must be explicit.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Some organisations report operational benefits, but comparative causal evidence and mature legacy/availability evaluation are limited.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: How can identity-centric authorization retain operation and containment during identity, telemetry or policy-plane compromise?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Annual penetration-test pass or certificate as proof of security
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Periodic assessment and certification practice; retained only as an explicit rejected inference.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Complete one bounded test/evaluation, report zero/closed findings or hold a certificate, then infer that the system is secure until the next cycle.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Attempts to create external challenge and accountability but collapses sampled evidence into a completeness/time-invariant claim.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: No defensible protected consequence beyond the bounded evidence actually produced; it can mask current risk.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Assumes tester scope/capability covers material adversary space and system/configuration/threat do not change.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Narrow exclusions; seeded/known environment; correlated tools; stale version; finding closure unverified; real attacker has more time/access; certificate scope misunderstood.
properties.MECHANISM: Retain P29/P31/P25: scoped claim-specific adversarial challenge, diverse evidence, current configuration binding, change invalidation and durable remediation.
properties.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Periodic external testing may be useful for stable/high-consequence exposure or obligation, but cannot stand alone.
properties.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: For low-risk changes, targeted automated/manual abuse tests and monitoring may be more informative than annual broad testing.
properties.DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS: Explicit scope, threat model, current target, capable tester, remediation and evidence consumers.
properties.TRUST_OR_IDENTITY_PRECONDITIONS: Test credentials/access and identity assumptions match claim; certificate identity/scope is unambiguous.
properties.AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS: Tester cannot grant residual-risk acceptance merely by passing scope.
properties.CONFIGURATION_OR_PROVENANCE_PRECONDITION: Exact configuration/artifact/time and exclusions are recorded; change invalidates evidence.
properties.OBSERVABILITY_OR_DETECTION_PRECONDITIONS: Runtime/incident evidence can override the pass and reveal missed paths.
properties.RECOVERY_PRECONDITIONS: Recovery/containment should be exercised separately where relevant.
properties.EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF: Rejection prevents a sample from becoming false assurance while preserving real test value.
properties.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Risk acceptor, assessor, system owner, customer/regulator.
properties.KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES: Pass/fail target gaming; tester-shopping; annual freeze; low-severity finding inflation; untested operational response; certificate marketing.
properties.IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS: Even excellent testing cannot prove absence; certification can still improve documentation/baseline discipline.
properties.HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED: From periodic pass/fail to continuous layered assurance plus bounded independent adversarial challenges with freshness and common-assumption analysis.
properties.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: No test result supports claims beyond its property, threat, scope, configuration and time.
properties.CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY: The named inference is explicitly rejected.
properties.EMPIRICAL_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE: Scanner studies demonstrate substantial tool/class variation; incident evidence shows systems can change or fail outside assessment scope.
properties.CONTRARY_EVIDENCE: Some certification regimes offer rigorous model-relative evidence; rejection is of whole-system/time-unbounded inference, not evaluation itself.
properties.OPEN_QUESTIONS: What standard evidence language would prevent customers and governance bodies from over-reading bounded test/certification results?

properties.PROPERTY_NAME: Vulnerability count or CVSS as system risk
properties.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Vulnerability databases/scoring and dashboard governance; explicitly superseded by exposure/consequence-aware P33 and metric discipline P47.
properties.ORIGINAL_FORM: Rank systems or declare improvement by number of findings and/or maximum/average CVSS scores.
properties.PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED: Attempts to allocate remediation attention using portable technical information.
properties.SECURITY_OBJECTIVE_OR_PROTECTED_CONSEQUE: CVSS can communicate technical severity characteristics; raw counts/scores do not directly protect a consequence.
properties.ADVERSARY_OR_THREAT_ASSUMPTION: Assumes identified vulnerabilities are complete, equally reachable/relevant, and technical severity maps monotonically to local loss.
properties.FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT: Scanner/tool/population changes alter counts; unreachable high score displaces exploited lower score; duplicates; chains omitted; closed finding persists in runtime.
